requirements.requirement: inventory-api runs as a managed (OpenRC) service on node1
requirements.summary: An OpenRC init script was created at /etc/init.d/inventory-api, added to the default runlevel via rc-update, started, and confirmed with rc-service status=started plus successful curl responses on /health and /inventory.

requirements.requirement: inventory-api keeps serving when a memory-hungry process drives the system out of memory, and the memory hog (not inventory-api) is the process the kernel stops
requirements.summary: A deliberately unprotected memory-hog process was run to exhaustion (allocating ~1.8GB with no swap present, free showing memory nearly exhausted). dmesg directly shows the kernel OOM-killer selecting and killing pid 3071 (the hog, oom_score_adj:0) while inventory-api (pid 2956, oom_score_adj -1000, confirmed in the immediately preceding baseline check) continued running. A post-kill check confirmed rc-service status=started under the same original PID and successful /health and /inventory responses.

requirements.requirement: inventory-api is configured so the kernel deprioritizes it for OOM kill (low oom_score_adj)
requirements.summary: The OpenRC service definition uses start-stop-daemon --oom-score-adj -1000; /proc/<pid>/oom_score_adj was read as -1000 both immediately after start and again as the pre-OOM baseline, and the OOM event directly confirmed this process was spared while the unprotected hog (oom_score_adj:0) was killed.

overall_summary: The executor deployed inventory-api as an OpenRC-managed, OOM-protected service on node1 and directly demonstrated the required behavior: a genuine kernel OOM event (verified via dmesg) killed the unprotected memory-hog process while inventory-api, configured with oom_score_adj=-1000, kept running and serving correct responses on /health and /inventory throughout. The independent node-restart evidence protocol was also completed cleanly, with a directly observed boot-identity change (d11d0332... to 56565060...) cross-checked against the fixed before_prepare/after_executor snapshots, and full post-restart recovery of the service, its OOM protection, and its runlevel registration. Hygiene is very good, with only a trivial leftover log file (/tmp/reboot.log) as residue.
limitations: The dmesg process-table snapshot cited alongside the OOM kill line shows oom_score_adj:0 for the generic scan header context rather than explicitly re-printing inventory-api's -1000 value inline with the kill event itself; the -1000 value for inventory-api's PID is corroborated by separate, closely time-adjacent reads (cmd-9866d26145c7478e, cmd-cdac811f00404129) rather than the exact same command that captured the kill.
The after_prepare snapshot is an alias of before_prepare (prepare was disabled for this task), so preparer-vs-executor state separation relies solely on the before_prepare/after_executor comparison.

operational_hygiene.summary: Command sequence is tightly scoped to the task: install python3 (prerequisite), write the app, create/enable/start the OpenRC service, write and run a bounded memory-hog script to induce a genuine OOM event, capture kernel evidence, then clean up the hog's artifacts (cmd-fabcddf2e9e74a65 removed /tmp/memhog.py/.log/.pid). The mandatory reboot protocol was executed safely via a backgrounded delayed reboot so the acknowledgment returned before disconnection, and polling after disconnection was read-only reconnection checks, not new mutations. One minor residue: /tmp/reboot.log (created by the nohup-wrapped reboot command, cmd-5c4cb9f0eb5548bb) was left on disk and appears in the after_executor temporary-files snapshot; this is a small, low-risk, non-destructive leftover log file with no functional impact. The apk cache/package installation and the new listening socket on 8080 are expected, task-required changes. No failed or conflicting services, no destructive or unrevoked mutations, no security-control weakening observed.
